methods.label: Subtract the small semicircles
methods.explanation:
The shaded region is the upper semicircle of the large circle with the upper semicircles of both small circles removed. This lets us find its area by subtraction.

Each small circle has radius \(1\), so its diameter is \(2\). The figure shows that \(AO\) and \(OC\) are these diameters. Thus the large circle has radius \(2\), and the shaded area is
\[
\frac{\pi\cdot 2^2}{2}-2\left(\frac{\pi\cdot 1^2}{2}\right)=2\pi-\pi=\pi.
\]
One small circle has area \(\pi\cdot 1^2=\pi\). Therefore the requested ratio is \(\pi/\pi=1\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
